sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Huron County?
sections.html:
Deeds for Huron County property are recorded at the Register of Deeds in Room 203 of the county building at 250 East Huron Avenue, Bad Axe, MI 48413. The phone is 989-269-9941 and the fax is 989-269-8786. The office keeps hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday except holidays, and it stays open through the noon hour.

The county's Register of Deeds page says land record indexes can be searched online from 1947 to the present. Older land records reaching back to 1848 are held in the office itself. Paper documents can be handed in or mailed, and the correct fee must arrive with them. The office takes checks, money orders, cash and credit cards.

sections.h2: Why do some old Huron County records start so late?
sections.html:
The courthouse fire of 1865 is the reason. Huron County was created by law on April 1, 1840 and fully organized on January 25, 1859. Sand Beach, now Harbor Beach, was the county seat until 1865, and when its courthouse burned in 1865 most of the records were destroyed. The seat moved to Port Austin until 1873, when the Board of Supervisors chose Bad Axe.

For a seller, the practical point is that a very old Huron County chain of title may have gaps. If a farm or lakeshore parcel has been in a family for generations, ask the title company early how it will handle the earliest records, and check the paper records in Room 203 where the indexes end.

sections.h2: How do I search Huron County land records before I list?
sections.html:
Start with the online indexes, which run from 1947 forward, and note the book and page or document number of your own deed. The county page also links to Laredo search information and to a Property Fraud Alert sign-up. Laredo is the software title searchers use to browse the official record, and the fraud alert tells an owner when a recorded document carries the exact name that was entered.

  • Pull your vesting deed and any mortgage so you know what must be discharged at closing.
  • Look for easements, land contracts and old assignments that touch the parcel.
  • Sign up for the fraud alert under the name on title, and add a second entry for any variation of it.
  • Call 989-269-9941 for records that predate the online index.

If a recorded paper turns up that you do not recognize, ask the staff in Room 203 to help you find it in the index.

sections.h2: What does Huron County charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
The standard Michigan charge is $30.00 per recorded document, whatever its page count, under MCL 600.2567. Michigan law adds a few smaller line items that a seller may meet:

  • $3.00 for each additional instrument that one assignment or discharge covers.
  • $5.00 to certify a recorded document.
  • $1.00 per page for copies of records.
  • 50 cents for each year searched in a grantor and grantee search, with a $5.00 minimum.

A fee is due when the document is left for recording. For electronic filings the statute allows payment within one business day. Huron County lists two e-recording companies on its page: Simplifile at 1-800-460-5657 and CSC at 1-866-652-0111. Call the register's office at 989-269-9941 to confirm the current amount for an unusual document.

sections.h2: What transfer tax comes with a Huron County sale?
sections.html:
The state tax is $3.75 for every $500 or fraction of the sale value under MCL 207.525. The county tax is 55 cents per $500 for a county of fewer than 2,000,000 people under MCL 207.504, and Huron County, at 30,530 people in the 2025 estimate, falls in that group. A deed must state the full value on its face, or an affidavit of value goes with it.

Worked example for a Huron County home priced at the county's median value
LineBasisResult
Median owner-occupied value (Census, 2020 to 2024)$154,300, rounded up to 309 units of $500309 units
State tax309 x $3.75$1,158.75
County tax309 x $0.55$169.95
Combined transfer taxSum of the two lines$1,328.70

The calculation is an illustration built from the statutory rates. Family transfers are one place the two acts differ. The state list in MCL 207.526 exempts a conveyance to a child or grandchild, while the county list in MCL 207.505 shows no such item. Ask the register of deeds how the county tax applies before a parent deeds a house to a son or daughter.

sections.h2: How should a deed be prepared for Huron County?
sections.html:
The recording statute, MCL 565.201 lists what the register of deeds may require. Run through this list with the title company or the drafter:

  • The printed name under each signature has to match the name in the notary's acknowledgment.
  • The notary's name must be printed or stamped on the same page near the notary signature.
  • Any deed signed after January 1, 1964 carries the name and business address of the person who drafted it.
  • The first five digits of a Social Security number must be removed or covered.
  • Papers in another language need a written English translation attached.

Once the office accepts and records a document, the statute treats it as conforming. A register of deeds may not reject a compliant instrument because of what it says.

sections.h2: What is Huron County like for people selling a house?
sections.html:
Huron County sits at the tip of the Thumb, with Saginaw Bay to the west and Lake Huron to the north and east, and more than 90 miles of shoreline. Of its 2,137 square miles, 836 are land. Agriculture is the leading industry, and visitors from Detroit, Flint and Saginaw come mostly to the Port Austin and Caseville area. Bad Axe is the seat and largest city, joined by Caseville and Harbor Beach, and Bay Port is a census-designated place. M-19, M-25, M-53 and M-142 are the state highways.

  • 30,530 people in 2025, down 2.8 percent from the 2020 base of 31,411.
  • 29.7 percent of residents are 65 or older.
  • 81.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied, with 14,150 households.
  • Median owner-occupied value is $154,300 and median household income is $58,870.
  • Only 69 building permits were issued in 2025.

sections.h2: Which other Huron County offices matter at closing?
sections.html: The Treasurer's Office is in Room 204 of the same building, phone 989-269-9238, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. without a lunch closure. The Equalization Department is in Room 306 at 989-269-6497, and Tax Mapping and GIS shares that room at 989-269-9421. Ask the Treasurer for the tax status of the parcel before the closing date so that any balance is paid from the sale.

faqs.q: What are the Huron County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., except on holidays, and it does not close at noon. It is in Room 203 at 250 East Huron Avenue in Bad Axe.

faqs.q: Does Huron County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes, the office takes e-recording through Simplifile and CSC. Contact either company directly, since they handle submission and the office receives the document electronically.

faqs.q: How far back do Huron County land records go?
faqs.a: Online indexes cover 1947 to the present, and records from 1848 on are held in the office. Records from the earliest years are thin because the 1865 courthouse fire at Sand Beach destroyed most of them.

faqs.q: Is a deed from parent to child exempt from transfer tax in Huron County?
faqs.a: The state tax has an exemption for conveyances to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild, but the county act's list does not show one. Call the register of deeds at 989-269-9941 before relying on any exemption, and state it on the deed.

faqs.q: What payment methods does the Huron County register accept?
faqs.a: Checks, money orders, cash and credit cards are accepted, and the correct fees must come with every recording. Checks can be made payable directly to the Register of Deeds.
